newsitem.title: USA: UK firm may bid for Carter-Wallace - report.
newsitem.headline: UK firm may bid for Carter-Wallace - report.

text.p: Carter-Wallace Inc may soon receive a $24 per share acquisition bid from a British suitor, according to Business Week magazine.
In its May 26 issue, the magazine said a British firm that makes packaged goods, foods and detergents will make the bid, which CPI Development Corp, Carter's majority shareholder, will "embrace."
A spokesman for Carter-Wallace, a personal-products maker, refused to comment on the Business Week report.
Shares of Carter-Wallace rose 3-5/8 to 17-1/2 in afternoon trade on Friday.
Business Week did not name the interested British firm.
In December, CPI Development rejected a $20 per share offer from billionaire investor Marvin Davis.
CPI owns about 35 percent of Carter-Wallace common stock, and about 95 percent of Carter-Wallace Class B shares, which represent 10 votes a piece.

CPI is a personal holding firm with three members, Carter-Wallace chairman and chief executive Henry Hoyt Jr, Hoyt's sister Suzanne Garcia and Richard Cruess, a professor at Canada's Mcgill University.
